newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEAGUE TO HEAR FROM EXPANSION CANDIDATES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEAGUE TO HEAR FROM EXPANSION CANDIDATES.

text.p: Nine cities vying for NHL expansion franchises will be making presentations to league officials Monday and Tuesday during meetings of the Board of Governors.

Eleven groups are scheduled to make pitches, as three different syndicates are seeking a franchise in Houston. Other cities applying are Atlanta; Columbus, Ohio; Hamilton, Ontario; Minneapolis-St. Paul; Nashville, Tennessee; Norfolk, Virginia; Oklahoma City and Raleigh-Durham, North Carolina.
No timetable for reviewing the bids has been set. The fee for new franchises is expected to be at least $75 million.
NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said last month that the league could add as many as four new teams, but stressed that expansion will not occur before the 1998-99 season.

Atlanta, home to the Flames in the 1970s before the team moved to Calgary, is considered the frontrunner for an expansion team. The NHL, eyeing a more lucrative television contract in two years, is expected to look favourably on the Atlanta bid made by Ted Turner and Time-Warner.

The NHL has expanded by five teams in the 1990s. The San Jose Sharks entered the league in 1990. The Tampa Bay Lightning and Ottawa Senators began play in 1991 and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and Florida Panthers joined the NHL two years later.
